Subject: Credential strategy & next steps for embedding + tool calls

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and three suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary / what we heard
- You want embeddings + a reranker for search over customer docs, and a small set of tool-calling workflows (structured outputs) from the same API surface.
- Security requirement: keys must be rotated automatically, audit logs captured, and the ops team prefers not to have long-lived bearer keys sitting in app config.
- Deployment target: initial PoC in AWS (dev/stage/prod), possibility of private VPC later.

Authentication options (high level) — see attached "redwood_auth_options.pdf" for a matrix:
1) Scoped API keys (fastest) — per-environment keys with limited scopes (embedding-only, generation-only). Easy to onboard but requires careful rotation and vaulting.
2) Service accounts + JWTs (recommended for server-to-server) — short-lived tokens minted by your KMS/identity provider with automatic rotation and auditable issuance. Good for backend-only workloads and aligns with your no-long-lived-key preference.
3) OAuth / user-delegated flows — for actions where the end user must authorize (less likely for your use-case).

Specifics for your stack
- Embeddings/reranker: we recommend service accounts with short-lived JWTs and a per-tenant key policy so you can revoke access quickly if needed.
- Tool calls / structured output: same token can be used as long as scopes are enforced at token mint time (e.g., scope=embedding,scope=tool_call).
- Rotation: propose automatic rotation every 7 days for PoC, with HSM/KMS integration for private deployment.

Immediate next steps
- (A) Tech workshop (30–45m) with our infra engineer to walk through sample JWT flows + SDK snippets — can you do Wed/Thu this week?
- (B) Share your current identity provider (Okta/Workday/other) and whether you prefer us to demonstrate JWT minting or API-key scoped flow.
- (C) I’ll attach a lightweight integration checklist to help your SRE team prepare (attached).

Attachments: redwood_auth_options.pdf; integration_checklist.csv

Best,

Thanks, Olga — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Preference: We lean toward service accounts + short-lived JWTs. Our security policy forbids long-lived secrets in config unless behind a vault and rotated automatically.
2) KMS: We use AWS KMS and an Okta-backed identity provider. We can mint tokens via a small service that our SRE team owns.
3) Reranker data: the reranker will be fed PII-stripped customer docs; want to confirm that token audit logs will show which service-account issued the calls (we need per-tenant tracing).
4) On-prem: We might require a private deployment later; curious how key management differs for Private (VPC/on-prem) vs Hosted.

Hi all — quick technical notes ahead of Wed’s workshop. Attaching an expanded snippet pack to the shared Drive; pasted two small examples below.

1) Service-account JWT (mint -> use) — minimal flow (pseudo-curl):

# Mint short-lived JWT from your token service (Okta-backed)
curl -X POST https://auth.example.com/mint 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <okta-service-account-token>" 
  -d '{"aud":"api.redwood.com","scopes":["embedding","rerank"],"exp":3600}'

# Use returned token against Redwood API
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <redwood-jwt>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"input":"summarize..."}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings

Notes:
- Redwood will validate aud + scopes and reject with 403 + error code SCOPE_MISSING if a requested endpoint requires a scope not present on the token.
- Audit log entry emitted for each request: {service_account_id, tenant_id, scope_list, model, request_id, timestamp} (we’ll show examples in the workshop).

2) Scoped API key approach (fast PoC):
- Create per-env keys in our console with explicit scopes (embedding-only). Keys can be rotated via API; recommend storing keys in your vault (HashiCorp Vault / AWS Secrets Manager).

Private (on-prem) notes:
- For Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS/HSM so you never expose raw key material. Token issuance happens inside your network; Redwood’s control plane can be configured to accept signed JWKS from your IdP.

I’ll bring a short demo that intentionally triggers SCOPE_MISSING and shows the error body + steps to fix.

Attachments referenced: full_sdk_snippets.zip (on shared Drive), sample_audit_log_examples.json

Thanks — see you Wed.
Dylan
Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
